clue.text: Dog eating two thousand caterpillars? Only one!

definitions.note: the plural is taken back at once: a single grub of the kind meant

indicators.note: a dog eating something takes it inside, so these letters go into the word for dog

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
the number spelt out
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A dog wolfing down a couple of thousand caterpillars, corrected by the setter to just the one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two thousand' reads as one number but splits in two. The plural 'caterpillars' is taken back by 'Only one!', so a single grub is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a moth larva that cuts through plant stems at soil level, a kind of caterpillar.

clue.text: Hat on old Mafia boss

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A hat perched on an elderly Mafia chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Capo is the Italian title for the head of a Mafia family or crew.

clue.text: Thought badly and used 23 4 ineffectively?

definitions.meaning: disapproved of something, held a low opinion
a photographer misusing an exposure gauge would get a dark, underexposed picture

explanation.surface: Someone disapproving and fumbling a photographic gadget in the same breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 4 is the linked answer LIGHT METER; the second reading takes the idiom literally, as a picture taken too dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means regarded with disapproval; literally it suggests a gloomy photographic shot.

clue.text: Like the supreme ruler with the ultimate in sumptuous loose attire

parts.note: a supreme ruler is over all others, read as the single word for top or total

indicators.note: the ultimate of a word is its final letter, here of sumptuous

explanation.surface: A monarch dressed in something luxurious and flowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Overalls are baggy protective garments worn over ordinary clothes.

clue.text: See 23
Remain at Oxford maybe and don't retire

parts.note: to stay is to remain
a student in residence at a university such as Oxford is said to be up

explanation.surface: Advice to an Oxford don to keep working rather than retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you 'go up' to a university such as Oxford and are 'up' while in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: Not going to bed, retire meaning turn in for the night, is keeping awake late.

clue.text: The lowly worker — being released, he'd plod on

indicators.note: letters let go from the phrase are dropped out of it

parts.note: a drudge does menial work
the letters of this contraction, H, E and D, are the ones removed

explanation.surface: A menial labourer, freed from work, keeps trudging along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being released' takes H, E and D out of THE DRUDGE in turn, leaving T and RUDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge is to walk heavily and wearily, keep plodding along.

clue.text: Accusation delivered to silent person that is so obvious!

definitions.meaning: a charge made against someone who never speaks
a sarcastic reply to stating the obvious

explanation.surface: Someone scolding a mute person, then sneering at a statement of the obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase accuses someone of silence; idiomatically it mocks a remark as stale news.

clue.text: Joke this bad keeps chaps hiding?

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: the reworked letters hold the next piece inside them
something gone bad is spoiled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: A groan-worthy joke that makes the men in the audience hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' scrambles the word 'this' to ISHT before the chaps go inside. 'hiding' is not concealment but a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a beating, a form of penalty for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Quality of authentic meal being reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by speech, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a proper tea, in British usage an evening meal done properly

explanation.surface: A judgement on the quality of a genuine meal, as described by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'tea' can mean an early evening meal, and 'a proper tea' is a hearty one.
explanation.definitionFit: A property is a characteristic or attribute of something.

clue.text: Gold container — on the inside black and a sort of red

indicators.note: the following letter is put within the container word

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
an urn is a vessel
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: A gold vessel lined with black, with a reddish tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Auburn is a reddish-brown colour, usually of hair.

clue.text: Bits of mischief with Left ousting Right to establish political platforms

indicators.note: one letter pushes the other out and takes its place

parts.note: pranks are mischievous tricks

explanation.surface: Left-wing troublemakers displacing the Right to set up their manifesto.
explanation.definitionFit: A plank is one policy in a party's platform, so these are its component policies.

clue.text: Displaying guile, Oscar is terribly irreverent

indicators.note: done terribly means done in a jumbled way, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Oscar, being sly, is behaving disrespectfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' looks like an intensifier for 'irreverent' but rearranges GUILE, OSCAR and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrilegious means treating sacred things with disrespect, profane.

clue.text: Like a tight garment for Spooner, being deceptive

indicators.note: the clergyman Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words

parts.note: with the next word this describes clothing that clings to the backside; this part gives the body word
a tight garment is said to be hugging the body

explanation.surface: A clinging garment that flatters to deceive.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening B and H of BUM HUGGING to get the deceiving word.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbugging means tricking or hoaxing people, putting on a show of falsehood.

clue.text: Old-fashioned printer needed this — as in lithographic op? Yes?

definitions.text: Old-fashioned printer needed this — as in lithographic op? Yes?

parts.words: Old-fashioned printer needed this — as in lithographic op? Yes?
parts.note: a printing-room device that held the text being set, and the closing words themselves hold the letters C, OP, Y in a row

explanation.surface: A query about what kit an old-time printer used in lithography.
explanation.walkthrough: Read across 'lithographiC OP? Yes' and you find COPY held in the words: the phrase itself is what it names.
explanation.definitionFit: A copyholder was a stand or clip keeping manuscript pages in view for a compositor.

clue.text: Obstructive international organisation attended by soldier wearing flashy stuff

parts.note: UNO is the United Nations Organization

indicators.note: the soldier is inside the jewellery, as one is in clothes one wears

parts.note: bling is showy jewellery
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A UN body accompanied by a soldier dripping in jewellery proves unhelpful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unwilling to help or cooperate is to be awkward and obstructive.

clue.text: Venue offering good game of golf?

parts.note: a round is one game of golf

explanation.surface: A golf course offered as a good place to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports ground is a place where matches are held, a venue.

clue.text: Hooligan facing test, all about being female, not ladylike

indicators.note: turned all about means the whole run of letters faces the other way

parts.note: a yob is a lout
the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for cars

explanation.surface: A thug up before a test, hearing about a woman who behaves unladylike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all about' reverses the whole of YOB plus MOT. 'being' here is a noun, a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomboy is a girl who acts in ways thought boyish rather than dainty.

clue.text: See 2
See 17
Like the Queen's coach, moving her onwards

indicators.note: letters on the move change places, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The royal coach carrying her forward on its procession.
explanation.definitionFit: The state coach is pulled by a team of horses, not motorised.

clue.text: Drinks in barrels dodgy dealer smuggled in ship

indicators.note: goods smuggled in are taken inside, so the dealer goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS means steamship
a tout sells tickets at inflated prices

explanation.surface: Kegs of beer brought aboard by a shady trader.
explanation.definitionFit: Stouts are dark beers, often served from casks.

clue.text: Take a risk, as a tree surgeon might?

definitions.meaning: to put oneself in an exposed position
an arborist literally climbs out along a branch

explanation.surface: A tree surgeon venturing out along a bough.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stake oneself on a risky position; literally it is climbing out along a branch.

clue.text: Eminent person came face to face with the monarch — photographer's got it?

parts.note: a leading light is an eminent figure
met means encountered
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A dignitary meeting the sovereign, with a photographer snapping the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographer carries this instrument to gauge exposure.

clue.text: Traveller in a VW

explanation.surface: Someone travelling in a Volkswagen.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was a famed medieval explorer, and Polo is a Volkswagen hatchback.

clue.text: Old city band on the road

definitions.meaning: the rubber ring of a wheel that meets the road

explanation.surface: A musical group from an ancient city out on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyre was a Phoenician city; a tyre is the rubber band round a wheel.

clue.text: In one's element here!

parts.note: In is a chemical symbol, so the element belonging to In is meant

explanation.surface: Someone feeling perfectly at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In one's element' is an idiom for being comfortable, but In is read as the symbol whose element is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Indium is a soft metallic chemical element with symbol In.

clue.text: Herb providing revenue for the farmer, we hear?

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the phrase is matched by its sound

parts.note: agricultural money, agri- being the farming prefix

explanation.surface: A plant that earns the farmer some income.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrimony is a yellow-flowered plant of the rose family used medicinally.

clue.text: Loud crone holding gentleman back

indicators.note: read back means the letters are taken from the end to the start
the crone word holds the gentleman inside it

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman
sir is the title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A noisy old woman clutching a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud' here is about colours, not noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish means gaudy and showy, as loud colours are.

clue.text: What may help car to restoration of power

indicators.note: restoring means rebuilding, so these letters are put back in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something that might get a stalled car back up and running.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken-down car can be pulled along by another vehicle using this line.
